rules.accepted_credit_types: AMA PRA Category 1 Credit; AAFP credit (accepted since 2025); certain Board-sponsored activities when stated by the Board
rules.new_licensee_rule: First renewal: no CME if licensed less than 1 year; at least 15 hours (incl. required subjects) if licensed 1 year or more during the initial period.
rules.alternatives: Board certification/recertification alone does not satisfy the requirement. Full licensees in an approved GME program may count a year of GME as 15 hours (Rule 24.2.4).
rules.audit_note: No documentation filed at renewal; keep records 4 years. The Board may audit for up to 4 years. Missing CME requires a make-up plan (up to 120 days) with the renewal.

topics.who: All physicians: hospice, palliative care or pain management services
Physicians with a DEA registration or a pending DEA application (presumed to prescribe controlled substances)

rules.notes: Licenses run Dec 1 to Nov 30 of the second following year and are renewed in even-numbered years. Medical marijuana courses do not count toward the controlled substances hours.
rules.legal_basis: Vermont Board of Medical Practice Rules, Rule 24 (eff. 5/1/2024); 26 V.S.A. § 1400(b)

rules.notes: DOs are licensed by the separate Vermont Board of Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons (Office of Professional Regulation). Only CE within 2 years of the renewal date counts. Board rules (2015) refer to § 1836 for an osteopathic share; current § 1836(c) states none.
rules.legal_basis: 26 V.S.A. § 1836(c); Administrative Rules of the Board of Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons, Rules 3.6-3.7
rules.accepted_credit_types: CME approved by the AOA or a successor or equivalent organization approved by the Board; 1 quarter college credit = 10 h, 1 semester credit = 15 h; learner time only
rules.new_licensee_rule: Documentation is first required with the first renewal application after two years of licensure.
rules.audit_note: Random audits plus conditioned and late-renewing licensees; detailed documentation required if selected; up to 90 days for a corrective plan (3 V.S.A. § 129).
